answer:
# Review export

A copy of a code review as it stands now: its commit messages, then every thread in full. The reviewer tells you what to do with it.

Lines starting 'reviewer' are reviewers' comments, with the reviewer's name when it has one ('reviewer security-bot:'). Lines starting 'coding agent:' are replies. A thread's heading names its thread status (open, resolved or dismissed) and, for an open one, its thread state in parentheses: held, waiting, queued, working, replied or failed. A thread marked 'outdated' was written on code that changed since: its code block is the code then, not the file now.

## The decisions behind the code: the review's commit messages (1), oldest first

Each commit from the base to the branch. Read them to know why the code is as it is.

### Commit 1
second

## Threads that need an answer (10)

### Thread <id-1:8> — app.py:2 — open (waiting)
Code:
```
    return f'hello {name}'
```
reviewer Test: Why an f-string?
reviewer Test: And the name?
coding agent: It reads better.
reviewer Test: A follow-up, held too

### Thread <id-5:8> — long.py:20 — open (waiting)
Code:
```
line_18 = 180
```
reviewer Test: Why 180?

### Thread <id-7:8> — app.py:1 — open (waiting) — outdated: its code changed after the thread was written
Code when the thread was written:
```
def greet(nam):
```
reviewer Test: Typo?

### Thread <id-9:8> — app.py:2 (old side, before the change) — open (waiting)
Code:
```
    return 'hi ' + name
```
reviewer Test: Why was this concatenated?

### Thread <id-11:8> — long.py:7-8 — open (waiting) — outdated: its code changed after the thread was written
Code when the thread was written:
```
line_5 = 5
line_6 = 6
```
reviewer Test: Why 5 and 6?

### Thread <id-13:8> — app.py:2 — open (waiting)
Code:
```
    return f'hello {name}'
```
reviewer Test: No code sent

### Thread <id-20:8> — general thread (not tied to a line) — open (waiting)
reviewer Test: Opened during a run

### Thread <id-22:8> — app.py:4 — open (waiting)
Code:
```
    return f'hello {name}'
```
reviewer Test: Shown before the import

### Thread <id-24:8> — general thread (not tied to a line) — open (waiting)
reviewer Test: Held until I submit

### Thread <id-27:8> — general thread (not tied to a line) — open (held)
reviewer Test: Held, then live

## Other threads (1)

### Thread <id-3:8> — general thread (not tied to a line) — resolved
reviewer Test: Is this ready?
reviewer Test: Still?

## How to reply

Reply to a thread with: <dt-reply> <thread> "<answer>"
<thread> is the 8 characters after 'Thread'. Write only the answer: difftate posts it as a reply. A reply changes no thread status.
For an answer with quotes or several lines, pass it on stdin: <dt-reply> <thread> <<'EOF' … EOF
